question: Explain the difference between bubble sort and quick sort. When would you use each one?

keyPoints: Bubble sort has O(n²) time complexity, simple but inefficient for large datasets
Quick sort has O(n log n) average time complexity, uses divide-and-conquer
Bubble sort is stable, quick sort is typically unstable
Quick sort is preferred for most real-world scenarios due to better performance
expectedAnswer.explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent elements if they're in wrong order, making multiple passes through the array. Quick sort selects a pivot element and partitions the array around it, recursively sorting sub-arrays. Quick sort is generally preferred for its superior average performance.
